## Phosphagen (ATP-PC) System

The phosphagen, or ATP-PC, system uses ATP primarily for shortterm, high-intensity activities (1). This energy system is considered anaerobic because it does not require the presence of oxygen to metabolize energy. However, this energy system does not generate ATP for immediate use and has a low capacity for ATP stores. Since the phosphagen system cannot store large amounts of energy, it is the dominant energy system for high-intensity activities that last no longer than 20 - 30 s (1). If an activity lasts longer than 20 - 30 s, energy supply shifts to the glycolytic energy system.
